title: The Benefits of a Bi-Directional Flip-to-Mute Microphone for Clear Team Communication in Multiplayer Games
summary: Enhance your multiplayer gaming sessions with the Turtle Beach bi-directional flip-to-mute microphone, a game-changing feature engineered for precision ...
body_text: Your team's coordinating the final push when suddenly your mic picks up your neighbor's lawnmower, drowning out the crucial callout. Meanwhile, your teammate's flip-to-mute microphone seamlessly switches between crystal-clear communication and instant silence, giving them the tactical advantage. In competitive multiplayer gaming, clear voice communication in multiplayer games isn't just convenient; it's the difference between victory and defeat. Modern gaming headset mic features have evolved far beyond basic voice transmission. The combination of directional pickup patterns and intuitive mute controls creates a communication system that enhances team coordination while minimizing distractions. Whether you're coordinating strategies in ranked matches or maintaining focus during clutch moments, understanding how directional microphone gaming technology works can transform your multiplayer experience. Understanding Directional Microphones in Gaming What Makes a Microphone Directional? Directional microphone gaming technology centers around pickup patterns that determine how microphones capture sound from different directions. Unlike omnidirectional microphones that pick up sound equally from all sides, directional microphones focus primarily on sound coming from specific directions. The most common directional pattern in gaming headsets is the cardioid pattern, named for its heart-shaped pickup zone. Cardioid microphones are most sensitive to sound from the front while significantly reducing sensitivity at the sides and rear , providing approximately 67% noise reduction from off-axis directions according to Audio-Technica's technical documentation. This focused approach makes them ideal for competitive gaming communication where background noise rejection is crucial. How Cardioid Differs from Bi-Directional Patterns While some may assume gaming headsets use bi-directional microphones, it's important to clarify that gaming headsets predominantly use cardioid (directional) microphones rather than bi-directional ones. Bi-directional microphones have a "figure-8" pickup pattern that captures sound equally from front and back while rejecting sound from the sides, a pattern designed for face-to-face interviews rather than gaming applications. For gaming headsets, cardioid patterns excel because they reject background noise while focusing on the user's voice, making them superior for team communication headset applications where environmental noise control is essential. The Flip-to-Mute Function Explained Instant Communication Control The flip-to-mute microphone mechanism represents one of the most intuitive controls in gaming audio. This design allows users to quickly mute their microphone by simply flipping the boom arm upward, providing immediate control over voice transmission during dynamic gaming situations. Turtle Beach headsets feature sophisticated flip-to-mute systems across their product lineup. The Stealth 700 Gen 3 incorporates a unidirectional flip-to-mute microphone with AI noise reduction technology, ensuring clear voice transmission when active and complete silence when muted. Minimizing Background Noise Interruptions A gaming headset with flip-up mute functionality serves a dual purpose: immediate mute capability and physical noise reduction. When flipped up, the microphone moves away from your mouth, reducing breath noise and inadvertent sound pickup. This physical separation, combined with the directional pickup pattern, creates multiple layers of noise control. The Stealth Pro and Atlas Air models demonstrate how premium noise-cancelling gaming mic technology integrates with flip-to-mute controls to provide professional-grade communication clarity. According to technical specifications, cardioid microphones can provide up to 20 dB less sensitivity at 180 degrees off-axis compared to on-axis , significantly reducing background noise interference. Stealth™ Pro Headset View Product Benefits of Team Communication Clearer Voice Transmission Best microphones for online gaming applications prioritize voice clarity above all else. Cardioid microphones in gaming headsets focus on the user's voice while minimizing environmental interference, ensuring that crucial callouts and strategic communications come through clearly to teammates. Turtle Beach's latest generation headsets incorporate advanced microphone technology. The Stealth 700 Gen 3 features completely redesigned unidirectional microphones with AI noise reduction to ensure optimal voice clarity. The directional nature of these microphones means your voice reaches teammates with enhanced clarity and consistency, unlike omnidirectional patterns that might capture room echo or ambient noise. Reduced Distractions During Gameplay Voice clarity in multiplayer games extends beyond just sound quality; it's about communication efficiency. When your microphone accurately captures only intended speech while rejecting background noise, teammates receive cleaner audio signals that require less mental processing to understand. This clarity becomes crucial during intense gaming moments when split-second communication can determine match outcomes. The combination of directional pickup patterns and flip-to-mute controls ensures that only intentional communication reaches your team, eliminating distracting background noise that could interfere with strategic coordination. Better Team Coordination in High-Stakes Matches The precision of directional microphones allows for enhanced team coordination through: Instant callouts without background interference Strategic discussions that remain private when muted Environmental awareness is maintained through reduced audio processing demands Consistent communication quality regardless of player movement or positioning The Stealth 500 and Recon 70 demonstrate how effective directional microphone implementation enhances team coordination across different gaming platforms and environments. Competitive Edge in Multiplayer Games Split-Second Communication Advantages In competitive gaming, advanced gaming headsets provide adjustable settings for microphone sensitivity and communication optimization. According to audio engineering principles , directional microphones offer a distance factor (DF) of 1.7 compared to omnidirectional microphones at 1.0, meaning they can capture desired sound sources from greater distances while maintaining the same signal-to-noise ratio. Directional microphones provide several competitive advantages: Reduced latency in voice processing due to cleaner input signals Enhanced clarity during rapid-fire callouts and strategic discussions Consistent performance across various gaming environments and noise conditions Professional-grade communication that matches industry standards Impact on Strategy and Team Performance Team communication headset technology directly influences strategic execution. When team members can communicate without background noise interference, strategic complexity increases. Teams can execute more sophisticated plays, coordinate timing with greater precision, and maintain situational awareness without audio distractions. The integration of flip-to-mute functionality adds another strategic layer. Players can instantly switch between private discussion and team communication, coordinate with specific teammates, or maintain focus during critical moments without completely disconnecting from team audio. Turtle Beach's Advanced Microphone Technology AI-Enhanced Noise Reduction Turtle Beach has pioneered AI-powered noise reduction in gaming headsets. The Stealth 700 Gen 3 incorporates advanced AI algorithms that analyze incoming audio in real-time, distinguishing between voice communication and background noise. This technology ensures that only intended speech reaches your teammates while environmental sounds are filtered out. The Atlas Air features similar advanced microphone technology , demonstrating Turtle Beach's commitment to clear communication across its product range. These AI systems adapt to different environments, providing consistent performance whether you're gaming in a quiet room or a more dynamic household setting. Cross-Platform Communication Excellence Turtle Beach headsets excel in multi-platform environments. The Stealth 700 Gen 3's CrossPlay Wireless Audio System includes dual USB transmitters, allowing seamless platform switching while maintaining microphone quality consistency. This ensures that whether you're communicating on PC, PlayStation, or Xbox, your voice clarity remains professional-grade. The Stealth Pro takes this further with advanced wireless technology , has a low-profile transmitter station, delivers a lag-free 2.4 GHz wireless connection, and serves as the charging station for the battery packs. Plus, an additional built-in USB-A port lets you charge your game controller or other devices.. Additional User Benefits Privacy and Ease of Use Gaming headset mic features like flip-to-mute provide essential privacy control during extended gaming sessions. Whether you need to handle personal conversations, respond to household situations, or simply take breaks from team communication, the intuitive flip motion provides instant privacy without complex button combinations or settings adjustments. The physical nature of flip-to-mute controls offers tactile feedback that doesn't require visual confirmation. This allows players to maintain focus on gameplay while making quick communication adjustments based on situational needs. Comfort and Seamless Integration Turtle Beach headsets integrate flip-to-mute microphones into ergonomic designs that prioritize extended comfort. The microphone boom positioning allows for optimal voice pickup while maintaining comfortable spacing from the user's mouth, reducing breath noise, and ensuring consistent audio quality. The Recon 70 exemplifies this approach with lightweight construction and comfortable positioning that works effectively across gaming sessions lasting several hours. Noise-cancelling gaming mic systems that work efficiently reduce the cognitive load associated with communication management, allowing players to focus entirely on gameplay strategy and execution. Technical Specifications That Matter Understanding Microphone Sensitivity According to professional audio documentation , cardioid microphones achieve their directional properties through carefully engineered acoustic chambers that create controlled sound pressure differences. This engineering results in maximum sensitivity at 0 degrees (directly in front) and minimum sensitivity at 180 degrees (directly behind). Turtle Beach leverages these acoustic principles in its headset designs. The Stealth series incorporates precision-engineered microphone capsules that optimize this directional response for gaming environments, ensuring maximum voice pickup efficiency while minimizing unwanted environmental noise. Frequency Response Optimization Professional gaming communication requires microphones optimized for human voice frequencies. Audio engineering research shows that cardioid microphones provide consistent frequency response within their acceptance angle, typically maintaining uniform sensitivity within 90 degrees of the on-axis position. Turtle Beach's advanced microphone systems are specifically tuned for gaming voice communication, ensuring that critical frequency ranges for speech intelligibility are accurately captured and transmitted to teammates. Making the Right Choice Evaluating Your Gaming Needs The best microphone for online gaming selection depends on your specific gaming environment and communication requirements. Consider factors like: Gaming environment noise levels and acoustic challenges Team communication frequency and complexity requirements Platform compatibility across your gaming ecosystem Comfort requirements for extended gaming sessions Additional features like wireless connectivity and battery life Professional vs. Casual Gaming Applications Competitive players prioritize competitive gaming communication features that provide measurable advantages in team coordination and strategic execution. Casual gamers might focus more on comfort and ease of use while maintaining good communication quality. The Turtle Beach headset collection offers options across this spectrum , from entry-level models with essential flip-to-mute functionality to professional-grade systems like the Stealth 700 Gen 3 with advanced noise cancellation and wireless capabilities. The Communication Advantage Voice clarity in multiplayer games represents a fundamental competitive advantage that extends far beyond basic audio quality. Directional flip-to-mute microphones provide the precise control and clarity needed for effective team coordination while maintaining the simplicity required for intensive gaming sessions. As gaming continues evolving toward more team-based, strategic experiences, communication technology becomes increasingly crucial for success. The combination of directional pickup patterns, intuitive mute controls, and professional-grade audio processing creates communication systems that enhance both individual performance and team effectiveness. Whether you're climbing ranked ladders, competing in tournaments, or enjoying casual multiplayer sessions, investing in quality directional microphone technology provides lasting benefits that improve every aspect of your gaming communication experience. Turtle Beach's commitment to advanced microphone engineering ensures that their headsets deliver the communication clarity and reliability that modern gaming demands. FAQ What is a directional microphone in gaming headsets? A directional microphone uses a cardioid pickup pattern to focus primarily on sound from the front while rejecting background noise from the sides and rear. This creates clearer voice transmission and reduces environmental distractions during team communication. How does flip-to-mute work on a gaming headset? Flip-to-mute allows you to mute your microphone by flipping the boom arm upward and unmute by flipping it down. Turtle Beach headsets provide audio feedback to indicate mute status, eliminating the need for visual confirmation. Why is a directional mic better for team communication? Directional microphones focus on your voice while rejecting background noise, providing clearer communication to teammates. This reduces distractions and ensures that strategic callouts and coordination communications come through clearly during intense gaming moments. Does a flip-to-mute microphone reduce background noise? Yes, flip-to-mute functionality provides both electronic muting and physical noise reduction. When flipped up, the microphone moves away from your mouth, reducing breath noise and inadvertent sound pickup while completely muting transmission. Which type of mic is best for multiplayer games? Cardioid (directional) microphones are ideal for multiplayer games because they focus on your voice while rejecting environmental noise. This provides clearer team communication and reduces distracting background sounds that could interfere with strategic coordination. Is a flip-to-mute microphone worth it for casual gamers? Yes, flip-to-mute provides valuable privacy control and communication management for all gaming levels. The intuitive design allows quick muting during personal conversations or breaks without complex controls, making it beneficial for both casual and competitive gaming.

title: Alector Announces Topline Results from Latozinemab Phase 3 Trial in Individuals with Frontotemporal Dementia Due to a GRN Mutation and Provides Business Update
summary: SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. , Oct. 21, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alector, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALEC), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing therapies to counteract the devastating progression of neurodegeneration, today announced results from the Phase 3 INFRONT-3 clinical trial
body_text: SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Oct. 21, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Alector, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALEC), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing therapies to counteract the devastating progression of neurodegeneration, today announced results from the Phase 3 INFRONT-3 clinical trial evaluating latozinemab (AL001) in individuals with frontotemporal dementia due to a progranulin gene mutation (FTD- GRN ). In the 96-week, double-blind INFRONT-3 trial, latozinemab, developed in collaboration with GSK, did not meet the clinical co-primary endpoint of slowing FTD- GRN progression, as measured by the Clinical Dementia Rating® plus National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Sum of Boxes (CDR® plus NACC FTLD-SB). Although treatment resulted in a statistically significant effect on the biomarker co-primary endpoint of plasma progranulin (PGRN) concentrations, the secondary and exploratory endpoints, such as fluid biomarkers and volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (vMRI), demonstrated no treatment-related effects on FTD- GRN . Preliminary safety data have not highlighted any major safety concerns at present. More in-depth analysis of the data is ongoing. “While latozinemab did not demonstrate a clinical benefit in INFRONT-3, the insights gained are invaluable for understanding progranulin-related neurodegeneration," said Giacomo Salvadore, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of Alector. "We extend our deepest gratitude to the patients, caregivers, and investigators who made this trial possible, and we plan to share the results with the scientific community to support continued progress in understanding progranulin biology and FTD pathophysiology.” Based on these results, the open-label extension portion of the INFRONT-3 trial and the continuation study for latozinemab will be discontinued. The INFRONT-3 trial results will be presented at an upcoming medical congress. Alector Pipeline Outlook Alector remains focused on advancing a pipeline of programs designed to treat neurodegenerative diseases through mechanisms that remove toxic proteins, replace deficient proteins, and restore immune and neuronal function. In the ongoing collaboration with GSK, nivisnebart (AL101/GSK4527226) is being evaluated in PROGRESS-AD, a global, 76-week Phase 2 clinical trial in individuals with early Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Enrollment was completed in April 2025, and trial completion is expected in 2026. An independent interim analysis is planned for the first half of 2026. A key pillar of Alector’s focus is its proprietary blood-brain barrier (BBB) technology platform, Alector Brain Carrier (ABC). Built on the core design principles of versatility, tunability, and differentiated binding to a distinct region of the transferrin receptor (TfR), ABC is intended to support the targeted delivery of therapeutics to the brain and to optimize safety and efficacy at lower doses. The platform’s tunable TfR binding affinities allow adjustment of binding strength to align with the needs of diverse therapeutic cargos, including antibodies, enzymes, proteins, and siRNA, aiming to achieve efficient transport across the BBB with the goal of balancing brain uptake, potency, and safety. Alector is progressing multiple preclinical programs enabled by ABC and has selected lead candidate AL137 for its ABC-enabled anti-amyloid beta (Aβ) antibody program in AD, and AL050 for its ABC-enabled glucocerebrosidase (GCase) enzyme replacement therapy program in Parkinson’s disease (PD). The company is targeting submission of investigational new drug (IND) applications for AL137 in 2026 and for AL050 in 2027. Alector is also continuing to advance its ABC-enabled siRNA platform. The platform is being designed for peripheral dosing, offering the potential for more convenient administration compared with traditional intrathecal or intracerebroventricular delivery. The most advanced siRNA program is ADP064-ABC, targeting tau for the potential treatment of AD and FTD. Collectively, these programs reflect Alector’s continued commitment to advancing innovative approaches to treat neurodegenerative diseases. Alector Executive Leadership and Business Update To align resources with these strategic priorities, Alector is reducing its workforce by approximately 49%. This is intended to focus the company’s resources on its highest-priority programs and to ensure continued progress across its portfolio. Alector thanks all employees affected by these measures for their dedication and contributions to the company’s mission. In parallel, Sara Kenkare-Mitra, Ph.D., President and Head of Research and Development (R&D), has resigned from her role, effective December 22, 2025, to pursue new leadership opportunities. She will remain with Alector until then to ensure a smooth transition and continuity across the R&D organization. The company is deeply appreciative of Dr. Kenkare-Mitra for her leadership and impactful contributions to Alector. “Sara has been an extraordinary builder and operator who transformed Alector into a mature, fully integrated R&D organization,” said Arnon Rosenthal, Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Alector. “Her sage leadership has been critical for the successful execution of our preclinical and clinical pipeline programs. Sara’s integrity and vision have left a lasting mark on the science, culture, and people at Alector, and we wish her continued success in her next chapter.” Alector estimates that it had approximately $291.1 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of September 30, 2025, which the company expects will provide runway through 2027. Alector plans to issue guidance for 2026 when it reports fourth quarter and full year 2025 financial results. About INFRONT-3 INFRONT-3 ( ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT04374136) was a pivotal, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of latozinemab (AL001) in slowing disease progression in individuals with frontotemporal dementia due to a progranulin gene mutation (FTD- GRN ). The trial enrolled symptomatic and at-risk FTD- GRN participants at multiple sites across North America, Europe, Argentina, and the Asia-Pacific region. The primary analysis was conducted in symptomatic participants only, in alignment with regulatory guidance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA). Based on the FDA’s recommendation, Alector and GSK amended the statistical analysis plan in the U.S. to include plasma progranulin (PGRN) concentration as a co-primary endpoint along with the Clinical Dementia Rating® plus National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Sum of Boxes (CDR® plus NACC FTLD-SB). This designation of plasma PGRN as a co-primary endpoint does not apply outside the United States. Participants were randomized to receive 60 mg/kg of latozinemab or placebo intravenously every four weeks over the 96-week treatment period (Part 1, the double-blind period). Following completion of Part 1, participants could either enter a 10-week safety follow-up or roll over into a 96-week open-label extension (OLE) study. Those who completed the OLE had the option to roll over into a continuation study ( ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT06111014). About Alector Alector is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing therapies to counteract the devastating progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Leveraging the principles of genetics, immunology, and neuroscience, the company is advancing a portfolio of programs that aim to remove toxic proteins, replace missing proteins, and restore immune and nerve cell function. Supported by biomarkers, Alector’s product candidates seek to treat a range of indications, such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson's disease, and frontotemporal dementia. The company is also developing Alector Brain Carrier (ABC), a proprietary blood-brain barrier platform, which is being selectively applied to its preclinical and research pipeline. ABC aims to enhance the delivery of therapeutics, achieve deeper brain penetration and efficacy at lower doses, and ultimately improve patient outcomes while reducing costs. Alector is headquartered in South San Francisco, California. For more information, please visit www.alector.com . title: Why a 200 Million Keystroke Life Cycle Matters for Gamers and Streamers
summary: Experience the durability and performance of Turtle Beach keyboards built for a 200 million keystroke life cycle. With Easy-Shift [+]™ technology acting...
body_text: Your stream just hit its stride. Chat's popping, donations are flowing, and you're about to nail that clutch play, then your W key stops responding. Game over. Career setback. Reputation damaged. For serious gamers and streamers, 200 million keystroke durability isn't just a number on a spec sheet; it's the difference between equipment that supports your ambitions and gear that sabotages them. When every frame matters and every moment of downtime costs viewers, the lifespan of a gaming keyboard becomes a critical investment decision . Turtle Beach's Vulcan II keyboards represent the pinnacle of this durability philosophy , with TITAN II Optical switches durability rated for 200 million keystrokes, double the industry standard for exceptional long-term reliability. What is Keystroke Life Cycle? Keystroke life cycle refers to the total number of key presses a switch can handle before mechanical failure occurs. Most mechanical keyboard switches are rated between 50-100 million keystrokes, with manufacturers conducting exhaustive testing where each switch undergoes millions of simulated keystrokes to meet stringent durability standards. How key switches are rated for durability involves specialized testing machines that repeatedly press switches under controlled conditions. Premium mechanical switches can withstand extreme temperatures from -40°C to 180°C, as switches must endure various environmental conditions during shipping and storage. The rating process isn't arbitrary; it's based on real-world usage patterns projected over years of intensive use. However, it's important to understand that these ratings represent laboratory conditions without the dust, moisture, and environmental factors present in real-world usage. Why Durability Matters for Gamers and Streamers High-Intensity Usage Demands Professional users generate significant keystrokes daily, with typical users averaging around 11,000 keystrokes per day. Intense gaming sessions can produce thousands of additional keystrokes during extended play periods. For streamers broadcasting multiple hours daily, this translates to hundreds of thousands of keystrokes weekly. Gaming keyboard durability 200M becomes essential when you consider that competitive gamers often exceed typical usage patterns significantly. The WASD keys, spacebar, and Shift keys experience particularly heavy wear during intense gaming sessions. Performance Consistency Over Time While standard keyboards may develop inconsistent key registration after 2-3 years of heavy use, premium mechanical keyboards maintain precise actuation force and timing throughout their operational lifespan. This consistency is crucial for: Competitive Gaming : Frame-perfect inputs require a reliable switch response Streaming : Consistent typing feel maintains productivity during long broadcast sessions Content Creation : Reliable macro execution and shortcut commands Cost Efficiency Analysis Why the keyboard life cycle matters becomes clear through basic economics. A durable keyboard lasting 5-10 years costs significantly less than replacing cheaper keyboards every 2-3 years. For professional streamers where equipment downtime directly impacts revenue, durability represents business continuity insurance. Technology Behind 200 Million Keystroke Life Cycle TITAN II Optical Switch Innovation Turtle Beach's TITAN II Optical switches achieve their exceptional 200 million keystroke durability through advanced optical actuation technology. Unlike traditional mechanical switches that rely on physical metal contacts, optical switches use light beams to register keystrokes, eliminating the primary wear point. This optical actuation eliminates the primary wear point in traditional switches, metal-on-metal contact, resulting in: No contact bounce or electrical degradation Consistent actuation force throughout the switch's lifespan Ultra-fast response times with minimal latency Immunity to dust and debris interference Pre-Lubed Stabilizers Benefits Pre-lubed mechanical switches in Turtle Beach keyboards include factory-applied lubrication on stabilizers, providing immediate benefits: Reduced friction and noise during keystrokes Smoother key travel and more consistent feel Extended switch lifespan through reduced mechanical wear Professional-grade performance out of the box The Vulcan II Mini Air exemplifies this technology , combining 200 million keystroke optical switches with pre-lubed stabilizers for tournament-ready performance. Real-World Impact on Gamers and Streamers Professional Usage Scenarios Data entry professionals average 15,000 keystrokes per hour during active typing periods. Gaming streamers combining gameplay, chat interaction, and content creation can reach 10,000-15,000 keystrokes per hour during intensive streaming sessions. Consider these realistic scenarios: Competitive FPS Player : 50,000-100,000 keystrokes per week during practice and competition Full-time Streamer : 100,000-200,000 keystrokes per week across gaming, chat, and content creation Professional Content Creator : 150,000+ keystrokes per week during intensive editing and streaming periods Long-Term Performance Reliability Long-lasting gaming keyboard technology ensures consistent performance across years of intensive use . Real-world testing shows that while switches may reach their rated limits, keyboards often experience other component failures first, including keycap wear, cable degradation, or PCB issues. Realistic Lifespan Expectations For 200 million keystroke durability , realistic expectations include: Heavy Professional Users (100,000+ keystrokes/week) : 5-8 years of reliable service Enthusiast Gamers (50,000+ keystrokes/week) : 8-12 years of consistent performance Casual Users (25,000+ keystrokes/week) : 10-15+ years with proper maintenance These estimates account for real-world factors like environmental conditions, usage patterns, and component wear beyond just switch degradation. Competitive Advantage Mechanical keyboard longevity for gamers translates directly to competitive advantages: Consistent muscle memory development over the years No performance degradation during crucial tournaments Reliable macro execution for complex strategies Predictable tactile feedback for frame-perfect timing Choosing the Right Keyboard for Longevity Key Features for Durability When evaluating keyboard switches for streaming and competitive gaming, prioritize these elements: Switch Technology : Optical switches like Turtle Beach's TITAN II provide superior longevity compared to traditional mechanical switches. The elimination of physical contact points significantly extends operational life. Build Quality : Look for keyboards with reinforced aluminum top plates, like those found across Turtle Beach's keyboard lineup. Metal construction provides structural integrity and protects against wear and tear. Keycap Material : PBT keycaps resist shine and wear better than ABS plastic. Modern mechanical keyboards use high-quality PBT material for keycaps, known for durability, matte finish, and resistance to wear and oils. Maintenance Tips for Extended Life Pre-lubed stabilizers require minimal maintenance, but following these practices maximizes keyboard lifespan: Regular Cleaning : Dust removal 2-3 times weekly and thorough cleaning every 2-3 months maintains optimal switch operation Proper Storage : Avoid extreme temperatures and humidity Gentle Usage : Consistent typing pressure prevents premature wear Cable Management : Proper cable routing prevents connector stress Professional-Grade Options Turtle Beach offers comprehensive solutions for different needs: Vulcan II Max : Full-size with 200M keystroke TITAN II switches Vulcan II Mini : Compact 65% layout for competitive gaming Vulcan II Mini Air : Wireless with ultra-long battery life Each model features the same 200 million keystroke durability standard, ensuring consistent reliability across the entire lineup. Environmental Factors and Real-World Considerations While 200 million keystroke durability represents exceptional engineering, real-world keyboard lifespan depends on multiple factors beyond switch ratings. Environmental conditions like dust accumulation, humidity, and temperature variations can affect overall keyboard longevity. Additionally, keyboards experience uneven wear patterns; certain keys like the spacebar, Enter, and gaming-specific keys (WASD) receive significantly more use than function keys or number pad keys. This uneven distribution means that high-use keys may show wear before others, regardless of the overall switch rating. Professional users should consider these factors when evaluating equipment investments, understanding that while 200 million keystroke switches provide exceptional durability, practical lifespan depends on usage patterns, maintenance, and environmental conditions. Investment in Your Gaming Future 200 million keystroke durability represents more than technical specifications; it's an investment in consistent performance, professional reliability, and long-term value. For serious gamers and streamers, choosing equipment with proven longevity eliminates performance anxiety and equipment-related setbacks. When your success depends on every input registering perfectly, when your audience expects uninterrupted content, and when your practice time is too valuable to lose to equipment failures, the choice becomes clear. Turtle Beach's commitment to 200 million keystroke durability across their keyboard lineup ensures your equipment supports your ambitions rather than limiting them. Don't let inferior equipment sabotage your potential. Invest in proven durability, advanced technology, and the peace of mind that comes with knowing your keyboard will perform reliably for years to come. FAQ What does a 200-million keystroke life cycle mean in a gaming keyboard A 200-million keystroke life cycle means each switch is tested and guaranteed to function properly for 200 million key presses under laboratory conditions. This represents exceptional durability, typically translating to 5-12 years of reliable performance depending on usage intensity. The Vulcan II Max exemplifies this durability standard. How long does a 200-million-stroke keyboard last for gamers For intensive users generating 100,000+ keystrokes weekly, expect 5-8 years of reliable service. Enthusiast gamers with moderate usage (50,000 keystrokes weekly) can expect 8-12 years of consistent performance. The Vulcan II Mini Air provides this exceptional longevity in a wireless format. Why is keyboard durability important for streamers Streamers depend on consistent equipment performance for professional broadcasts. Keyboard failures during live streams can interrupt content, disappoint audiences, and impact revenue. Durable keyboards like the Vulcan II Mini ensure reliable performance during extended streaming sessions. What are TITAN II Optical switches TITAN II Optical switches are Turtle Beach's proprietary optical actuation technology that uses light beams instead of physical contacts to register keystrokes. This eliminates the primary wear point in traditional switches, enabling 200 million keystrokes of durability with consistent performance throughout the keyboard's lifespan. How does a keyboard's keystroke life cycle affect gaming performance Higher keystroke life cycles ensure consistent actuation force, timing, and tactile feedback throughout the keyboard's operational period. This consistency is crucial for developing muscle memory, executing frame-perfect inputs, and maintaining competitive performance over years of use with Turtle Beach keyboards . Can a mechanical keyboard really last 200 million keystrokes Yes, through rigorous testing with specialized machines that simulate years of intensive use. Optical switches like Turtle Beach's TITAN II technology eliminate physical wear points, enabling verified 200 million keystroke durability. However, real-world lifespan also depends on environmental factors, maintenance, and usage patterns beyond just switch degradation.

title: Connect an AI Agent to Jira tickets
summary: Let your Quickchat AI Agent search your Jira tickets and answer questions based on them, a step by step guide
body_text: Introduction In this blog post, I will show you how to connect your AI Agent to Jira. We will be using: a Jira account ( free ) a Quickchat’s AI Agent ( sign up here and use for free ) Looking for the canonical, continuously-updated reference? The same walkthrough lives in our docs at docs.quickchat.ai/channels/jira . This post is the long-form, narrated version. It will enable your Quickchat AI Agent to: be able to search through your Jira tickets, and be smart about answering questions based on them We will use Quickchat’s AI Actions (custom HTTP actions) to let your Agent call the Enhanced search for issues endpoint of the Jira (Atlassian) API. Craft an AI Agent creative about interpreting user inputs Watch the Video How it works Here is how your AI Agent will operate during conversations: User asks a question like “what’s up with issues to do with mercury?” AI Agent fetches relevant information from the Jira API using a query like “mercury” AI Agent replies to the user based on the information fetched from the API Please follow the steps below. The whole setup shouldn’t take longer than 10 minutes ! Step 0 - create a Jira account and project Go to id.atlassian.com/signup , create and verify your account. Add Jira to your Atlassian apps (the free plan will be enough to start). Set up your first project and create tickets like in the example below. Example board with Jira issues Step 1 - Jira API authentication token Go to id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens and create your API token which will look something like this: ATATT3xFfGF01sKUl0HEW2-_-u9umfLSz7jeblmeLzEHZ1DLcdLbKeVF137iTHGkKhPuNMSKX8mkbwLpHXT4-qXEn-xNEnfiK8_XDVW6XXvGd_SBV3HD4kJInGNjfg2_yEoJFN6uwy4NRqeuhV2tjmyzxozLBRn35OhXkDA6QGfLFvf2_PKuNtA=8DA704E4 In order to be able to use your Atlassian API token in Quickchat AI Actions, you need to base64-encode it along with your email address: your_email@example.com:ATATT3xFfGF01sKUl0HEW2-_-u9umfLSz7jeblmeLzEHZ1DLcdLbKeVF137iTHGkKhPuNMSKX8mkbwLpHXT4-qXEn-xNEnfiK8_XDVW6XXvGd_SBV3HD4kJInGNjfg2_yEoJFN6uwy4NRqeuhV2tjmyzxozLBRn35OhXkDA6QGfLFvf2_PKuNtA=8DA704E4 Make sure to include the exact email address you used to set up your Atlassian account You can use a simple online tool like base64encode.org . Make sure to use the Live mode which guarantees the encoding happens entirely in your browser. You can use a free online tool to encode your API token Alternatively, here is how to do it on your machine in a simple python script : import base64 email = "your_email@example.com" api_token = "ATATT3xFfGF01sKUl0HEW2-_-u9umfLSz7jeblmeLzEHZ1DLcdLbKeVF137iTHGkKhPuNMSKX8mkbwLpHXT4-qXEn-xNEnfiK8_XDVW6XXvGd_SBV3HD4kJInGNjfg2_yEoJFN6uwy4NRqeuhV2tjmyzxozLBRn35OhXkDA6QGfLFvf2_PKuNtA=8DA704E4" credentials = f " { email } : { api_token } " b64_credentials = base64.b64encode(credentials.encode( "utf-8" )).decode( "utf-8" ) print ( f "Basic { b64_credentials } " ) The above script will give you a ready-to-use header with the encoded token which looks something like this: Basic eW91cl9lbWFpbEBleGFtcGxlLmNvbTpBVEFUVDN4RmZHRjAxc0tVbDBIRVcyLV8tdTl1bWZMU3o3amVibG1lTHpFSFoxRExjZExiS2VWRjEzN2lUSEdrS2hQdU5NU0tYOG1rYndMcEhYVDQtcVhFbi14TkVuZmlLOF9YRFZXNlhYdkdkX1NCVjNIRDRrSkluR05qZmcyX3lFb0pGTjZ1d3k0TlJxZXVoVjJ0am15enhvekxCUm4zNU9oWGtEQTZRR2ZMRnZmMl9QS3VOdEE9OERBNzA0RTQ= Step 2 - create a Quickchat AI Action In the Quickchat AI app , go to Actions & MCPs and add an action: AI Action page Give your AI Action an appropriate name: Name : Search Jira issues Insert AI Action name Step 3 - set input parameters Your AI Agent’s main task will be to translate what the user is asking about into an exact query to use to search through Jira issues. When it comes to searching for issues Jira recently fully migrated to JQL (Jira Query Language) to allow for performing more complicated search. This allows your AI Agent to be much more powerful. Set up your input parameters as follows: Format Name Description Default value Required Text jql (see below) - ✅ In order to achieve great performance with your AI Agent, a well-crafted description is hugely important: Description: A single valid JQL (Jira Query Language) string built per the description. Favor recall: prefer `(text ~ "term1" OR text ~ "term2")` over chaining with AND, and use parentheses for grouping. For "not started / in progress / done" questions, filter on `statusCategory` ("To Do", "In Progress", "Done"), which is stable across projects; use `status = "..."` only when the user names a specific status that exists on the board. Avoid custom fields. Examples: `statusCategory = "In Progress" AND (text ~ "mercury" OR text ~ "venus")`, `(text ~ "planet*" OR text ~ "integration")`, `project = "Solar System" AND statusCategory = "To Do"`. A well-crafted parameter description is key for AI Agent performance A note on Jira statuses Jira separates a status name from its category , and JQL treats them differently: The status name is whatever the board shows. One project uses To Do / In Progress / Done , another uses Open / In Review / Closed . The status category is one of three fixed buckets every status maps to: To Do , In Progress , Done . status = "To Do" filters by name, so it returns nothing on a board whose first column is named Open . This is a common reason an agent confidently reports “no tickets to do” while the board is full of them. For “what has not started”, “what is in progress” and “what is done” questions, filter on the category instead: statusCategory = "To Do" statusCategory = "In Progress" statusCategory = "Done" Keep status = "..." for when the user names a specific status you know exists on the board. You can also list your board’s real status names in the Action description (Step 7) so the agent maps a request like “ready for QA” to the right one. Step 4 - set API endpoint URL Select GET as the Action Type Set the endpoint URL to the Jira /rest/api/3/search/jql endpoint Set your API endpoint URL Make sure to use your Atlassian domain name . You will find it in your Jira board URL. Your Atlassian domain name Step 5 - set API request headers Define your API request headers as follows: Accept Autorization application/json Basic cGlvdHJAcXVpY2tjaGF0LmFpOkFUQVRUM3hGZkdGMGlQOVNacEhVZ1o5YUJfWGhmQjZJWjJId3MyaHlsMzEtTlNpYW90Z2tZVzRxQXEwQ3R4UVY1OXFTZkpWWVZNcXlxem42MWRkR0VobmJWNzdzaWtrb19ZWkhtLUgwazFOZGh4WlpQMnltYmZ1SzhBRmlFMnJEUmdqd182N1hkSFFUelFQY2I2U1lrNUFPRlRuVnZvaGxkZUd3djVpM2VrcEFyMVJ4QnJWRncyYz04MEZGQTcyMA== Pay special attention to correctly formatting your Authorization header: Basic <base64-encoded email:api token> Set your API request headers Step 6 - set API request query parameters Set two query parameters for your AI request: jql is taking a dynamic value defined earlier in the What to ask the user first section. It is the AI Agent’s job to fill out the value of this parameter based on what the user has said in the conversation. fields is taking a fixed value. For each Jira issues, we are only interested in its summary , description and status . jql fields {{jql}} summary,description,status Set your API request query parameters Make sure the jql parameter correctly points to the value defined earlier. You can select it from the Add AI Data dropdown menu. Select the dynamic jql parameter from the dropdown menu Step 7 - set API Action description The final crucial ingredient of a well set-up AI Action is its description. While the AI Agent has a good understanding of your API endpoint just from its URL and parameters, it is key to optimize its behaviour for your use case . The three most important aspects included in the prompt are: when to invoke the action — listing every phrasing the user might pick (find / search / look for, as well as explain / tell me about / describe / what is / how is the status of) so the agent does not skip the call when the user does not say “search” suggestions on how to use the advanced JQL syntax when searching for Jira issues how to handle empty results — the agent must say so explicitly rather than refuse access Here is the resultant API Action Description : Use this action whenever the user asks anything that could be answered by data in their Jira — projects, issues, statuses, sprints, test cycles, descriptions, owners, comments — regardless of how they phrase the request (find / search / look for / explain / tell me about / describe / what is / how is the status of, etc.). Do not refuse access; query Jira first. Construct a JQL that prioritises recall over precision: prefer `(text ~ "term1" OR text ~ "term2")` over chaining with AND, and use parentheses for grouping. For lifecycle questions (not started, in progress, done) filter on `statusCategory` ("To Do" / "In Progress" / "Done") rather than `status`, because status names vary by board; use `status = "..."` only when the user names a specific status. Avoid custom fields. If Jira returns no matches, say so explicitly to the user and suggest a refined query. Step 8 - test the API Action Before we test the AI Action in conversation, we can test how the API itself is being called in the Test Response tab. Let’s do a first test with the following query which should return all issues in the project: project = "Solar System" Searching for all issues in the Solar System project Below is the test response we get. As expected, it lists the summary, description and status fields for all the 6 issues on our Jira board. Response lists all issues in the Solar System project Let’s try one more query. This time let’s search for all the issues which mention “mercury”: text ~ "mercury" Searching for issues which mention mercury We have now validated that the AI Action correctly calls our API endpoint. We can now move on to testing full conversations with the AI Agent! Step 9 - test the AI Agent in conversations Head back to the Quickchat AI app and test your AI Agent in conversation preview. Conversation #1 AI Agent gives a summary of all issues within the project In this simple conversation the AI Agent gives an overview of all the issues within the project. A look behind the scenes tell us that the exact query it ran against the API endpoint was: project = "Solar System" Conversation #2 AI Agent responds to questions about specific issues and statuses In this case, the AI Agent was asked about two separate aspects: a specific issue and issues ongoing in general. A look behind the scenes tells us that it decided to use the Jira API in a two-step process: Check if pluto is ongoing: status = "In Progress" AND (text ~ "pluto" OR text ~ "ongoing" OR text ~ "current" OR text ~ "active" OR text ~ "progress") Check what else is ongoing: status = "In Progress" Conversation #3 AI Agent responds to a creative query 😉 In this case I wanted to throw a curveball at the AI Agent and asked it a question that takes some creativity to interpret correctly. Here is how it got translated into a JQL query: (text ~ "planet" OR text ~ "upstream" OR text ~ "mercury" OR text ~ "venus") Try these phrasings To be confident the AI Action fires no matter how your end users phrase their request, run each of the prompts below against your test scenario. The agent should query Jira on every one of them, not just the search-style ones: “find all open issues about live scores” “search for issues with mercury ” “explain the Solar System project” “tell me about the open issues in this sprint” “describe what’s currently in progress” “what is the status of pluto?” If any of these phrasings does not invoke the AI Action, double-check that your API Action description (Step 7) lists those verbs explicitly. What to expect when Jira has no matching issues. When Jira returns zero results, your AI Agent should say so explicitly — for example, “I checked Jira and found no matching issues for your query — try a broader phrasing or remove the status filter.” If instead you see the agent reply with “I don’t have direct access to your Jira” , the AI Action did not fire at all. Re-check the description from Step 7 and confirm that it explicitly lists non-search verbs ( explain , tell me about , describe , what is ). Summary In this blog post, we showed how an AI Agent can be set up to use a specific API endpoint in a creative way in conversations. The correct setup doesn’t come out of the box - it requires providing detailed extra information of the specific use case we have in mind. Please feel free to reuse the prompts and descriptions shown in this blog post for creating your own similar AI Agents! For another fully worked example in the same step-by-step style, see how to connect your AI Agent to Google Sheets and log leads, unanswered questions, and demo requests to a spreadsheet. Want to keep this guide bookmarked? The canonical, continuously-updated version of this walkthrough lives in our docs at docs.quickchat.ai/channels/jira — head there to copy-paste the latest API Action description and to follow updates to the recipe. Going further A Jira action does not have to be a single fixed request. You can inject built-in conversation variables and saved metadata (such as the visitor’s language or values captured earlier in the conversation) into any field, and you can add several actions so the agent picks the right one per question. The AI Actions reference covers the full set of options. Related guides The same AI Action mechanism connects an agent to any HTTP API. Other walkthroughs that use it: Build an AI Discord moderation bot with custom AI Actions Connect your AI Agent to the Telegram Bot API Connect your AI Agent to Google Sheets Connect your AI Agent to HubSpot to log contacts, deals, and tickets Send Slack notifications with AI Actions Connect Cal.com to Your AI Agent in 5 Minutes How to create an AI Support Agent from your documentation AI Agent for SaaS Customer Support BONUS The above blog post was written by a human (yours truly) but could have just as well been written by AI. For example, by pasting a prompt like this one into ChatGPT: I need an API endpoint that allows me to search through my Jira tickets. Guide me through the process step by step so that it is accessible to a moderately technical person: - Provide links to documentation describing the endpoint - Any necessary account creation and initial setup - If any paid account is needed, indicate that clearly - If any authentication such as API tokens is needed, guide me through the process of creating them and show me exactly every step needed to be able to use them as an HTTP request header. For example, if base64 encoding is needed, show a script or another way of achieving that. - Show to me exactly what header keys and values I need for the HTTP request (show me header keys and values in a table) - Show to me exactly what payload parameters I need for the HTTP request (show me payload parameter name and example values in a table) In the future, perhaps rather than search through Jira tickets you would like to: send messages to a Slack channel? fetch information from a Notion page? perform an action via Zapier? Say that in the first sentence and run the prompt again! You will obtain perfectly good instructions to add the exact AI Action you need!

title: Whirlpool Corporation, Habitat for Humanity, and Indiana University Celebrate 15 Years of Collaboration with Landmark Build
body_text: Whirlpool Corporation, Habitat for Humanity of Monroe County, and Indiana University’s Kelley School of Business are marking a major milestone in their long-standing collaboration: 15 years of building hope and homes together in Bloomington, Ind. This year’s build constructed five new net-zero homes in Bloomington’s Osage Place neighborhood as part of the BuildBetter with Whirlpool program, emphasizing the company’s deep commitment to sustainable housing and community building. "At Whirlpool Corporation, we believe a home is the foundation of opportunity, stability, and well-being. For 15 years, our work with Habitat for Humanity and the Kelley School has enabled us to put that belief into action. This year’s expanded build is a milestone that reflects our long-term commitment to building thriving and sustainable communities." "At Whirlpool Corporation, we believe a home is the foundation of opportunity, stability, and well-being,” said Jim Peters, Whirlpool chief financial and administrative officer and Kelley School alumnus. “For 15 years, our work with Habitat for Humanity and the Kelley School has enabled us to put that belief into action. This year’s expanded build is a milestone that reflects our long-term commitment to building thriving and sustainable communities." The 2025 build, held the week of October 13, marked the completion of phase one of the Osage Place development, where nine of the homes, including the five net zero homes built this year, are climate resilient and energy-efficient BuildBetter with Whirlpool homes. In addition, the City of Bloomington has awarded $250k in grants for solar panels for 30 homes in this community to help continue the sustainable housing efforts from the BuildBetter with Whirlpool work. "Every home we build is more than just walls and a roof; it’s a step toward generational change for families,” said Wendi Goodlett, CEO of Habitat for Humanity of Monroe County. “Thanks to the unwavering support and the energy of Whirlpool Corporation and IU Kelley students, five more families will soon have a safe, affordable, and sustainable place to call home. Together, we are creating not just houses, but thriving neighborhoods that embody hope and resilience." Launched in 2021, the BuildBetter with Whirlpool program has supported the construction of 260 climate-resilient, energy-efficient homes across the U.S., delivering an average of 45% energy cost savings per family, compared to the average new home, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 15% per home. In the program’s current phase, it will deliver 50 net-zero energy or net-zero energy-ready homes in the next two years with features such as solar panels, high-efficiency heating and cooling systems and energy and water efficient appliances based on the homeowner and geographic needs. Volunteers remain at the heart of these builds, including Whirlpool employees, Monroe County Habitat for Humanity volunteers, and students from IU’s Kelley School of Business. Beyond construction, Whirlpool is also investing in workforce development by engaging IU students through professional development opportunities and hands-on building experiences. "This collaboration demonstrates the power of learning by doing,” said Pat Hopkins, dean of the IU Kelley School of Business and the James R. Hodge Chair of Excellence. “Our students don’t just study leadership and social impact in the classroom--they live it through meaningful projects like these builds. By working alongside Whirlpool Corporation and Habitat for Humanity, our students gain invaluable experience that will shape their futures while leaving a lasting mark on their community." For more info about Whirlpool Corporation’s support of Habitat for Humanity, visit whirlpoolcorp.com/HfH .

title: Craftwork's Expert Cabinetry Painting Process
summary: We believe in not just altering the appearance of your cabinets but revitalizing your entire space with precision, quality, and an artistic touch.
body_text: Craftwork's Expert Cabinetry Painting Process We believe in not just altering the appearance of your cabinets but revitalizing your entire space with precision, quality, and an artistic touch. Let's dive deep into the meticulous and transformative process of cabinetry painting. At Craftwork, we believe in not just altering the appearance of your cabinets but revitalizing your entire space with precision, quality, and an artistic touch. To ensure the process is as smooth and efficient as possible, here's a step-by-step guide on what you can expect for your cabinet painting project. Your Steps Towards Transformation Step 1: Get a Virtual Estimate At Craftwork, our estimate process is designed to provide you with a clear and concise pricing structure, tailored to the unique aspects of your cabinetry. We calculate the cost of our painting services based on the number of cabinet doors , drawers , and boxes within your space, as each element requires individual attention and detail. The box is defined as the structural area enclosed by the doors and drawers, which often involves detailed work to ensure a seamless finish. Additionally, the sheen level you select plays a crucial role in the pricing— with high-gloss finishes being the most premium due to the meticulous process required to achieve their distinctive, reflective quality. Here is an image showing a standard cabinet configuration. Standard cabinet configuration. Step 2: Schedule Your Project When it comes to scheduling your cabinet painting project, at Craftwork, we meticulously consider several factors to ensure the best possible experience for you. We take a close look at our calendar, factor in weather conditions that might affect the project, and align our most suitable crew's availability to guarantee top-notch service. Typically, most cabinet projects require about 5-7 days to complete. To make the process as convenient as possible for you, we recommend selecting a week that aligns well with your personal schedule and commitments. This proactive approach in choosing a suitable time frame helps us deliver the quality and efficiency Craftwork is known for, while also accommodating your needs and ensuring a smooth, hassle-free experience. Step 3: Choose Paint Colors and Sheen Selecting the right color and sheen is crucial for your cabinetry. Our kitchen cabinet paint guide has a wide range of color options, helping you pick shades that complement your space and style. Craftwork offers 3 sheens for cabinetry refinishing: Flat: Hides imperfections and offers a contemporary look/ Satin: Ideal for most cabinets, offering a smooth finish that’s easy to clean. High-Gloss Lacquer: Best for a modern, sleek look, though it's more prone to showing imperfections. If your cabinets were factory-finished, they were probably done with lacquer. Step 4: Prepare the Space Before our Craftwork team steps into your home to begin the transformation of your cabinetry, a little preparation on your end can make the process smoother and more efficient. Clear the Area: Remove all items from your countertops and the interiors of the cabinets. This step is crucial for giving us unobstructed access to the work area. Protect Your Belongings : We recommend moving any furniture in or near the project space. For larger pieces that can't be moved out, simply relocate them to the center of the room. Accessible Workspace : Please provide a clear pathway to and around the project area, allowing our team to move equipment and materials easily and safely. Electronics & Personal Items : We advise that you relocate any such items, as we cannot move electronics like TVs and computers. These will be worked around if left in the area, but moving them is preferable for their safety and ours. Pet Safety : We love our furry friends, but for their safety and to prevent any stress or accidents, please ensure they are kept in a secure area away from the work zone. Blue and white cabinets Day-by-Day Breakdown: Day 0 - Space Prep Customer clears their drawers and cabinets, if possible. If we’re painting the interior of the cabinet, clear everything. Day 1 - Dismantling and Space Prep Cover all furniture with protective plastic and tape around faucets and appliances for protection. Floors are covered with protective sheets, with edges taped to prevent damage. Dismantle the kitchen, packing up drawers. Doors and drawers are transported to our warehouse for advanced spraying, ensuring a flawless finish in a controlled environment. This step is crucial for achieving superior quality. Day 2 through 4 - Sand & Prep Sanding and additional prep work on cabinet surfaces. Day 3 - Prime and Paint Prime cabinet boxes. Paint the cabinet boxes and clean the area thoroughly. Day 4 - Reassembly Reassemble the kitchen, restoring all elements to their original positions. Additional Notes: The kitchen will be out of use for 3 days. Potential wall paint touch-ups due to taping.
